hero.title: Astrophotography, decoded.
hero.description: A short guide to the frames you should be capturing and what AstroStack actually does to them — written for first-time astrophotographers.

primer.title: A single frame is mostly noise.
primer.description: Camera sensors generate thermal noise, vignette toward the edges and accumulate dust on every optical surface. Calibration frames measure those defects so the stacker can subtract them — and stacking many lights averages out the random noise the calibration can't remove.

frames.title: Every astrophoto is a stack of these.
frames.description: Lights are your data. Darks, flats, dark-flats and bias are calibration frames that tell the stacker how to clean each light up.

light.name: Light frames
light.purpose: The actual photons from your target — every faint nebula tendril or galaxy arm comes from these subs.
light.exposure: Longest exposure your mount can track without star trails (60 s – 5 min typical).
light.notes: Captured during the imaging session itself. More integration time = cleaner final image.

dark.name: Dark frames
dark.purpose: Map the thermal signal and hot pixels generated by the sensor when it heats up during long exposures.
dark.exposure: Identical exposure, ISO/gain and sensor temperature as your lights, lens cap on.
dark.notes: Build a dark library you can reuse across sessions, but only while temperature, exposure and gain stay matched.

flat.name: Flat frames
flat.purpose: Reveal vignetting, dust motes and uneven illumination across the optical train so they can be divided out.
flat.exposure: Short exposure aimed at a uniform light source (sky panel, T-shirt method, dawn sky).
flat.notes: Must be captured without disturbing focus, camera rotation or filter — recapture if anything in the imaging train moves.

darkFlat.name: Dark-flat frames
darkFlat.purpose: Calibrate the bias and read noise specifically present in your flat frames.
darkFlat.exposure: Same exposure as your flats, lens cap on. Often replaces bias frames for CMOS sensors.
darkFlat.notes: Only valid alongside the flat library they were taken with — store them together.

bias.name: Bias / Offset frames
bias.purpose: Capture the read-out noise floor of the sensor — the signal present even in a zero-second exposure.
bias.exposure: The shortest exposure your camera supports, lens cap on.
bias.notes: Build once per camera/gain combination and reuse for months. Modern CMOS workflows often skip bias in favour of dark-flats.

reuse.title: What invalidates a calibration library?
reuse.description: The good news: most calibration frames can be reused for weeks or months. The bad news: a handful of changes silently make them useless, so the rules below are worth memorising.

lights.invalidatedBy: Always single-use — they are the data of one specific session.

darks.invalidatedBy: Sensor temperature drift, exposure change, ISO/gain change.
darks.shelfLife: Months, if temperature is regulated (cooled cameras).

flats.invalidatedBy: Focus shift, camera rotation, filter swap, dust motes moving.
flats.shelfLife: Single imaging-train configuration, typically one night.

darkFlats.invalidatedBy: Anything that invalidates the flats they belong to.

bias.shelfLife: Long-term — months to years per camera/gain pair.

pipeline.title: What AstroStack does to your stack.
pipeline.description: Each session runs through these ten steps in order. You can resume from any failed step without re-running the ones that already succeeded.

rawConversion.title: RAW → FITS conversion
rawConversion.description: Decodes camera RAW files (CR2, NEF, ARW, DNG…) into the scientific FITS format expected by every downstream tool, preserving the full bit depth of the sensor.

preprocessing.title: Calibration & stacking
preprocessing.description: Builds master darks, flats and bias from your calibration frames, applies them to every light, registers the subs on the same star pattern and stacks them to dramatically improve the signal-to-noise ratio.

plateSolving.title: Plate solving
plateSolving.description: Identifies the exact patch of sky your image covers by matching star positions against an astrometric catalog. Coordinates and orientation are written into the FITS header and used by later steps.

gradientRemoval.title: Background gradient removal
gradientRemoval.description: Detects and subtracts the smooth light-pollution and Moon glow gradients that wash out faint structures, leaving a flat, neutral background to stretch from.

stretchColor.title: Stretch & colour calibration
stretchColor.description: Re-maps the linear sensor data into a viewable image: faint nebulosity becomes visible, while photometric colour calibration uses catalog star colours to set a scientifically neutral white balance.

denoise.title: AI noise reduction
denoise.description: A neural network trained on astrophotography data smooths out background grain without softening real stars or nebula details — far gentler than generic photo denoisers.

sharpen.title: AI sharpening / deconvolution
sharpen.description: Recovers detail lost to seeing, focus and tracking imperfections. Stars become tighter and structures crisper without amplifying noise.

superResolution.title: AI super-resolution (2×)
superResolution.description: Doubles the linear resolution of the frame using a model trained to hallucinate plausible high-frequency detail — useful for small targets or short focal lengths.

starSeparation.title: Star separation
starSeparation.description: Splits the image into a starless layer and a stars-only layer so each can be processed independently. This is the trick behind most modern nebula renderings where stars feel small but the gas glows.

export.title: Export
export.description: Writes the final master to FITS (for re-processing), TIFF (for editing) and JPEG (for sharing), and renders a thumbnail for the gallery.

tips.title: Six habits that will save you a night.
tips.description: The advice astrophotographers wish someone had handed them on day one.

focus.title: Nail focus first
focus.body: A Bahtinov mask takes thirty seconds and is the single biggest jump in star quality you can get for free.

dither.title: Dither between subs
dither.body: Small random offsets between exposures let stacking reject hot pixels and walking noise — your darks do less work and the result is cleaner.

captureOrder.title: Capture order
captureOrder.body: Lights first, then flats before you tear down the rig (so the optical train is undisturbed). Darks and bias can be shot any time the sensor temperature matches.

matchCalibration.title: Match calibration to lights
matchCalibration.body: Same exposure, same ISO/gain, same temperature for darks. Same focus and rotation for flats. Mismatches add noise instead of removing it.

brightTargets.title: Start with bright targets
brightTargets.body: M42 (Orion), M31 (Andromeda), M45 (Pleiades) and the Veil Nebula forgive short integration times and tracking errors — perfect first projects.

profiles.title: Profiles over fiddling
profiles.body: Pick a Quality preset and let the pipeline run end-to-end before you start tuning. Compare runs, then adjust one parameter at a time.
